commitResults.messageBody: Move file loading, saved-record validation, task reconstruction, and file writing out of MEKA into a dedicated Storage class. MEKA now coordinates persistence through a small load/save interface while retaining its existing recovery behavior when loading or saving fails. This establishes the first cohesive OOP boundary without changing commands, console output, or the saved-data format.

Introduce a TaskList domain class to own task ordering, one-based lookup validation, addition, deletion, iteration, and task counts. Update MEKA and Storage to exchange TaskList instances instead of exposing ArrayList as their shared application model. This prepares command objects to operate on a focused task-list abstraction while preserving the existing UI and persistence behavior.

Introduce a Ui class that owns command input and every user-facing console message, including the welcome banner, dividers, task listings, confirmations, and storage warnings. Update MEKA to coordinate through Ui methods instead of Scanner and System.out directly. This establishes the user-interface boundary required by A-MoreOOP and prepares command objects to report results without embedding presentation code.

Introduce a Parser class that recognizes command words, validates numeric and textual arguments, parses strict date-time values, and constructs todo, deadline, and event tasks. Simplify MEKA so it routes recognized commands and executes their effects without containing parsing details. Parsing failures now consistently use MekaException while preserving all existing user-facing messages.

Add an abstract Command contract with concrete add, delete, mark, unmark, list, and exit commands. Change Parser.parse to construct command objects and refactor MEKA into an instance-based coordinator whose run loop only reads, parses, executes, and handles errors. Move storage availability tracking into Storage so all mutating commands share the same execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage) interface while preserving session-only recovery after persistence failures.

Group commands, tasks, parsing, storage, UI, and exceptions by responsibility while keeping src/main/java as the source root. Rename the entry point to meka.Meka and update the usage and UI test commands for packaged compilation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge Gradle support after package organization
commitResults.messageBody:
The Gradle milestone branches from Level-8 and omits the OOP and
package increments. Rebuild the merge on A-Packages and configure
Gradle to launch meka.Meka while retaining the packaged source tree.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test core behavior in the packaged application
commitResults.messageBody:
The existing tests target default-package classes and miss the
extracted parser, storage, and task list. Move them into meka.task
and cover command execution, persistence, and validation through
the public APIs introduced by A-MoreOOP.

Name the Shadow JAR meka.jar and document building and running it.
Retain the meka.Meka entry point configured during the Gradle step.

Carry the JavaDoc increment into the extracted parser, task list,
and UI. Explain validation messages and exceptions, and complete
parameter and return documentation across the packaged classes.

Apply the coding-standard increment to the A-Packages structure.
Use a descriptive boolean name, immutable task descriptions, and
indented switch cases without flattening the package hierarchy.

Retain the project Java review rules while preserving the agreed
package hierarchy when applying the coding standard.

Retain the project Git conventions for future commits and branches
while rebuilding the coding-standard branch on the packaged base.

commitResults.messageBody:

TaskList, and Ui so the Level-9 feature preserves the OOP design.
Retain the console behavior and add coverage for empty, unmatched,
and mixed-case searches without changing saved tasks.

Merge JavaDoc improvements from the parallel increment branch
into the packaged application.

Combine coding-standard improvements with the JavaDoc increment
while retaining the agreed packages and both parallel branches.

Integrate find with the JavaDoc and coding-standard increments.
